sections.html:
Bethel Park is a home rule municipality in Allegheny County, about 7 miles south of Pittsburgh, with an estimated 32,074 residents on July 1, 2025. Homes are mostly owner-occupied at 76.4 percent for 2020 to 2024, the median home value is $273,400 and the median household income is $107,090. Only 92.9 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so turnover is low and well-kept houses get noticed. Median value covers the whole borough, so use it as background, not as a price for your street.

The municipal building is at 5100 West Library Avenue. The primary ZIP code is 15102, while 15234, 15236 and 15241 serve border communities, so confirm the municipality on the parcel record before you assume which rules apply.

There are 14,829 households averaging 2.19 people. Median monthly owner cost with a mortgage is $1,902, and median gross rent is $1,311. Most buyers are therefore owners moving up or in from nearby, who tend to care about condition and a clean sewer lateral report.

sections.h2: Dye test and camera lateral inspection
sections.html:
A seller in Bethel Park must complete a dye test and a camera lateral inspection before any deed is transferred. The Camera Lateral Inspections Ordinance took effect on January 1, 2025, and the municipality's dye test page lays out the rules.

  • Finish the dye test and camera inspection 21 days before closing or deed transfer.
  • The municipality charges a $50 processing fee.
  • The camera lateral inspection must come from a contractor certified by the National Association of Sewer Service Companies, and the plumber must be registered through the health department.
  • A plumber holding an Allegheny County license performs the dye test, and a municipal building code official signs off if a defect is corrected.
  • A test already performed and certified within the last two years can satisfy the rule.
  • A deed cannot be transferred until needed repairs are made and pass inspection.

Paperwork has a 48-hour turnaround. Request the forms through the municipal office at 412-831-6800, extension 205. An occupancy inspection is not required for a sale. Owners who deeded a property without the test receive an official letter, and non-compliance leads to a citation.

Because the deadline sits 21 days before closing, a sale that closes in under three weeks needs the dye test and camera work done before a contract is signed. Start by requesting the forms from the municipality, hire the certified plumber, and keep the video and paperwork together for the buyer's title company.

If the camera finds a defect, price the repair in early, because the deed cannot move until the repair passes inspection. A certified test from the last two years is worth locating if you have one, since it can save you the whole step.

1. Ask the municipal office at 412-831-6800, extension 205, for the dye test and camera forms.
  2. Hire an Allegheny County plumber and a camera contractor certified by the National Association of Sewer Service Companies.
  3. Get the paperwork back, which has a 48-hour turnaround, and fix any defect so it can pass inspection.
  4. Keep the video, the certification and the receipt for the $50 processing fee in one folder.
  5. Confirm the work is finished 21 days before the closing date.
  6. Check for open permits on past projects through Community Development.

A seller who works through this list before accepting an offer rarely has the deed held up at the end.

Bethel Park sits on the Pittsburgh coal seam, and all of the borough was undermined. The Pittsburgh Terminal No. 8 Mine, also called the H Mine and the Coverdale Mine, opened around 1920 and is closed.

Raise mine subsidence early in a sale. Ask your homeowner's insurer whether the policy covers mine subsidence, and ask the buyer's title company what it will search. Buyers who know the area will ask about coverage and about any past damage you are aware of, and a straight answer up front is better than a question at the inspection stage.

The municipality's development fee schedule, effective September 9, 2025, sets the amounts most sellers meet.

Permits go to the Community Development Department on the second floor of the municipal building, or by email to the permits address on the municipality's site. Residential questions go to extension 131 at 412-831-6800. Pennsylvania adopted the 2021 I-Codes under the Uniform Construction Code effective January 1, 2026, so repairs before a sale follow the newer code. Grass over 8 inches is a code violation, so mow before photos and showings.

sections.h2: How Allegheny County assessments and appeals work
sections.html:
Allegheny County's Office of Property Assessments sets values for Bethel Park, and appeals go first to the Board of Property Assessment Appeals and Review. A party who disagrees with that result can appeal to the Board of Viewers at the Court of Common Pleas.

  • Hearings take place by telephone.
  • Legal representation is optional, and an authorized representative may appear for the owner.
  • A taxing body, such as a school district or municipality, can also file an appeal on a property.
  • Special Appeals can be filed year-round in response to a written determination notice from the assessment office.

Call the Office of Property Assessments for the annual filing window, because the county sets it by ordinance. The county's real estate page also covers state and local realty transfer taxes, the municipal and school shares, and recording requirements for deeds.

Pittsburgh Regional Transit's three light rail lines run through the borough, with park-and-ride lots at South Hills Village, West Library, Lytle and Washington Junction. PA Route 88 and US Route 19 carry most commercial traffic. Interstate 79 and the Mon-Fayette Expressway stay outside the boundary, each about a 15-minute drive. Rail access is worth a line in a listing. Mean commute is 26.5 minutes, and buyers who work downtown often ask how close the nearest station is, so have the answer ready for showings and the listing description.

sections.h2: Ways to sell fast in Bethel Park
sections.html:
An owner here can list the house, sell privately or accept a cash offer. A cash buyer skips the lender's appraisal, but the sewer lateral rules still apply to the deed, so plan the dye test and camera work whichever route you pick.

Compare offers on what you keep after payoffs, repairs and any prorated taxes. Ask each buyer for proof of funds and a closing date in writing before you take the house off the market.

faqs.q: Do I need a dye test to sell my Bethel Park house?
faqs.a: Yes. Bethel Park requires a dye test and a camera lateral inspection before a deed transfers, unless one was done and certified within the last two years.

faqs.q: How much does the Bethel Park lateral paperwork cost?
faqs.a: The municipality charges a $50 processing fee. The plumber's fees are separate and depend on the contractor you hire.

faqs.q: Does Bethel Park require an occupancy inspection when a house is sold?
faqs.a: No. An occupancy inspection is not required for a sale. A $50 Certificate of Occupancy appears on the fee schedule for other situations.

faqs.q: Is Bethel Park built over old coal mines?
faqs.a: Yes. All of the borough was undermined, and part of it lies over the closed Pittsburgh Terminal No. 8 Mine.

faqs.q: Where do I appeal an Allegheny County assessment?
faqs.a: Appeals go to the Board of Property Assessment Appeals and Review. Hearings are held by telephone, and later appeals go to the Board of Viewers.
